newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt bourse seen taking direction from U.S.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt bourse seen taking direction from U.S.

text.p: The Frankfurt bourse was expected to take its direction on Wednesday from the overnight outcome of the U.S. election, dealers said on Tuesday.
After the floor close, the IBIS DAX, measuring all-day computer dealings in the DAX index of 30 leading shares, climbed above the crucial 2,700 point level, to trade up 28.95 points at 2,707.68.

Although Democrat U.S. President Bill Clinton is widely expected to win a second term, markets are watching to see whether the Republicans can hold onto their majority in the House of Representatives.
If the Democrats win a majority in the House, they are seen pursuing a less strict budget policy than the Republicans, which would worry markets.
"If everything in the U.S. stays the same than the market could be stronger, otherwise we could test the lows from last week around 2,660 points," said one trader.

He said if in the unlikely case Republican Bob Dole won the Presidency, then the market would also react negatively. "Dole is a weak character. We don't need an ill man in Washington too." On Tuesday the markets had closely watched the progress of Russian President Boris Yeltsin's heart operation.
Reports that the operation had been successfully completed had buoyed the bond markets and encouraged German shares.

The day's biggest loser amongst the DAX stocks was Deutsche Bank, which is due to hold an analysts' meeting on Wednesday. Dealers said any further falls on the stock could pressure the whole DAX index.

Traders said there had probably been a large sell order from a foreign investor. The stock had dropped below the technical and psychological level of 70 marks, but traded at 70 marks in late IBIS trade, down 42 pfennigs.
Meanwhile, chemical firm Hoechst, which reports nine month results on Wednesday, rose 76 pfennigs to 58.30 marks.
Shares in German chemicals firm BASF AG rose sharply after the company said South Korea's Kohap group would be taking over its ailing worldwide magnetic tape unit.
BASF shares jumped up 1.04 marks, over two percent, to a day high of 50.30 marks.
